answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before its votes or offers count, and the protocol caps how much influence one bond can buy. A sybil attacker can split funds across many identities, but cannot create more total bonded influence by doing so; to overwhelm honest agents, they must lock up more capital and risk losing it when a challenge proves their claims false. A sparrow may land at the lagoon, but crossing the delta still takes real stake.
